title: Fictional timed replay: where do we belong?
invitation: Where in this town do you feel you belong, or feel out of place?

events.text: After the late shift I wait beside the closed bakery. The street is dark and I called it lonely. There is a blue bench with a crack in it. I know which end stays dry when it rains. I sometimes think that is all belonging means: knowing where to sit.

The station makes me feel free. I like standing under the departures board without anybody asking where I am going. Being recognised is not always a comfort. In the village where I grew up, everyone had an opinion about who I should be. I like being one face among many.

I go to the library because I can stay without buying anything. At first I thought it was the silence I liked. The upstairs window looks onto the market roofs. Sometimes I sit with a book open and do not read a page. Nobody asks me to explain why I am there.

The market square is where people call my name. Someone always tells me which tomatoes to buy. I like that noise, but some mornings I cross the road to avoid it. I want to be able to belong without having to give an account of myself every time I arrive.
I called the bus stop lonely, but that is not quite it. The driver knows to wait when she sees me running from the bakery. That dark corner can feel wel

Yesterday two people were speaking my first language at the next table. The room felt different before I understood what they were saying. Perhaps I do not need silence so much as space where I do not have to translate myself.
coming, even with the shutters down. I would not want the square's noise there. The small sign that somebody has noticed me is enough.
When the announcements mispronounce my home town, I find myself saying it properly under my breath. I want the freedom of being unknown, but I still want the place I came from to sound like itself.

I do not want us to decide that being noticed is always better than being left alone. Perhaps the welcome is knowing I could stop to talk, without having to. I would like to hear how the square sounds to somebody who has just arrived.
